name: Tommy Robinson
role: English anti-Islam activist; founder of the English Defence League (2009-2013) and organiser of Unite the Kingdom rallies
summary: Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, known as Tommy Robinson, is a British activist whose work centres on opposing Islam, mass immigration and what he calls censorship and establishment cover-up of grooming gangs. He frames his politics as defence of British culture, Christianity and free speech, and rejects the 'far right' label; critics and many news outlets describe him as far-right. Most of his recorded positions concern immigration, Islam, national identity, free speech and Israel, so many economic and constitutional statements are unanswered.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Says people were jailed for social media posts and that the judiciary and media were 'weaponised' to silence the public; campaigns on free speech as one of his five core principles, and mocks hate-speech enforcement as applied selectively.

reduce-immigration.rationale: States he and his movement are 'against mass immigration' and argues for stopping further intake (e.g. no more Afghans); distinguishes genuine refugees from those arriving by small boat.

open-borders.rationale: Describes open-border immigration as an establishment agenda he opposes; says illegal arrivals are 'people trafficking' and the country must protect its own people first.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Repeatedly criticises 'zero assimilation' and lack of integration in Luton and says Christian immigrants 'would assimilate'; frames expected assimilation as a standard, though he also says he does not hate immigrants.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says Britons have been made ashamed, 'we've lost our identity, we've lost our culture', and organises Unite the Kingdom around British culture, identity and traditions.

elite-replacement.rationale: Says mass immigration is 'not a mistake' but a deliberate establishment policy (to lower wages, cause friction and weaken patriotism); he did not describe it as a plan to replace the native population, and a counter-terror officer's 'great replacement' question to him is not his statement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Repeatedly describes the British establishment, police, judiciary and media as corrupt and covering up abuse, and says it works to silence ordinary people.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said England is historically a white nation and 'has to remain a majority white country', comparing Japan remaining majority Japanese; separately rejects expulsion of non-whites and distinguishes himself from ethno-nationalists.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says Luton had no racial tension and was divided by religious lines, so he attributes conflict to religion and demographic change from Muslim immigration rather than race as such; he also says remaining majority white matters. Mixed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Calls Islam a violent, oppressive, supremacist ideology incompatible with Western freedom and democracy and calls Britain a Judeo-Christian culture, which rejects treating all cultures as merely different.

population-transfer.rationale: Asked whether he wants to deport all Muslims, said he never said that because it would mean deporting people he loves; he does say people who want to overthrow democracy must be dealt with.

traditional-family.rationale: Describes an organised attack on Christianity and the family, and says communities that keep the family unit do not have the problems he describes.

more-religion-public.rationale: Calls for a Christian revival and for reintroducing Christendom, Christianity and Jesus to British public life; says a country with no belief leaves a void; organised a Christmas service as part of Unite the Kingdom.

direct-votes.rationale: On recognition of a Palestinian state said it should be put to a democratic British vote; this is one instance rather than a general principle.

nation-first.rationale: Says Britain's job is 'not to help Afghanistan' but to protect British people first.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Says establishment open-border agenda works with the UN and EU, and approves of Israel not pandering to the United Nations.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Describes the EU, with the UN, as part of the establishment immigration agenda; Wikipedia says he voiced objection to EU 'oppression' on Russian state media in 2020.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Strongly defends Israel ('If Israel falls, we all fall'), praised its government for not backing down and visited at the Israeli government's invitation; never frames it as a stated right to a state in the Land of Israel in the sources opened.

national-rebirth.rationale: Says the culture is decaying, calls for a 'cultural revolution' and a 'Christian revival' to recover British identity.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Objects to asylum seekers housed in hotels and fed and clothed at public expense, and says to protect British people first; no explicit statement on welfare benefits for lawful immigrants.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said the two-child benefit cap should be kept ('I don't want to pay for' large families on benefits); does not make the dependency argument.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Says the country's job 'is not to help Afghanistan' but to protect British people first.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Campaigned for the family of Raif Badawi, jailed and sentenced to lashes in Saudi Arabia and pursued for apostasy, and describes him as having been treated unjustly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Condemns establishment control of media, campaigned against the BBC (called for the licence fee to be scrapped), and campaigns for free speech.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Opposes Sharia taking hold in Britain and urges US lawmakers to join an anti-Sharia caucus, which implies one civil law for all.

free-trade.rationale: Timcast: wanted Trump-style trade barriers protecting British workers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Timcast 00:09:23: backed tariffs to prevent manufacturing jobs leaving Britain.

political-violence-never.rationale: Triggernometry: condemned riots and said he called for peace and nonviolence.

consent-of-governed.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Triggernometry: wanted Qatari and Iranian funding of ideological institutions stopped.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Timcast: described Muslim communities organizing to supplant democratic government.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Timcast: defended Quran-burning speech against punishment and intimidation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: September: identified Islam itself, not just extremism, as incompatible.

notes:
Evidence is mainly long-form interviews (auto captions) and reported quotes; he has given little on economic policy. Positions at the EDL stage (e.g. 2013 Quilliam statement apologising for earlier remarks and rejecting violence) differ in tone from recent ones; most recent used.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; prior answers not read. Full Triggernometry and Brand transcripts, the February 2026 Timcast interview and September 2026 Freitas captions were downloaded and searched. Timcast has several speakers; only identifiable Robinson passages used. Freitas advertisements and host opinions excluded. The ten priority economic theories remain unknown: neither tariff advocacy nor criticism of corporations benefiting from migration establishes a general view of capitalism, public ownership, value theory or alienated labour. Welfare child caps are not a statement that all welfare creates dependency. Opposition to LGBT instruction is not opposition to all sex education, and liberal treatment of homosexuals is not a stated marriage policy. Visits and allies’ policies do not establish his positions. The Russia statement does not settle NATO withdrawal or support for invasion. Ecological and technological searches found no matching stated position; social-media use is not technological optimism. All remaining null statements reviewed. Earlier street violence is distinguished from political violence; participation by violent supporters is not attributed to him without evidence he directed it. Salience-only validation failure retained; no answers added to clear the gate. Self-defence remarks do not explicitly address killing, and rejection of Sharia does not establish a position on all scriptural law.
